General Description:
The Senior Clinical Research Associate (SCRA) is primarily a site monitor and is responsible for the management and oversight of their assigned clinical study sites to ensure data quality and patient safety in accordance with ICH-GCP guidelines, local regulations, and applicable SOPs.
The SCRA collaborates with the Clinical Study Teams (CSTs) by supporting day to day clinical study activities, departmental tasks, and provides mentoring to other CRA team members within established protocols and portfolio under general supervision.
Proactively seeks opportunities to lead and drive improvements to optimize effectiveness and efficiencies within the Site Management group as well as within the greater Americas region.

Essential Functions of the job:
• Perform and coordinate assigned aspects of the clinical monitoring process in accordance with GCPs and SOPs to assess the safety and efficacy of investigational products and/or medical devices
• Conduct site visits to determine protocol and regulatory compliance, and prepare required documentation
• Develop collaborative relationships with investigative sites, and study vendors
• Track enrollment status reports to ensure study sites stay on track to meet enrollment goals
• Track study-specific status reports to ensure all required information regarding site issues, deviations, and CRF status are kept current by the monitoring team
• Serve as mentor/trainer for less experienced CRAs to assist with general and study-specific monitoring issues
• Provide direct support to the Clinical Study Manager by assisting with monitoring visit report review and other managerial tasks as needed
• Perform study-specific training with project team
• Develop study-specific monitoring tools and forms for use by monitoring team to assist in efficient review of study data
• Perform Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reconciliation and work with study sites and CRAs to resolve discrepancies
• Review outstanding data reports and work with CRAs to ensure data collection is met per contractual guidelines
• Works with Clinical Trial Oversight Managers (CTOMs) and Clinical Study Team (CST) to manage site trends through dashboard review and ongoing risk assessment to ensure quality standards and address concerns associated with study delivery at sites within established protocols and portfolio under general supervision
• Collaborates with CST and clinical study sites to ensure timely delivery of study milestones (i.e., study startup, recruitment, database analyses, closeout, etc.).
• Provide support for study sites, and CRAs with audits/inspections preparation/responses and quality issues, as needed, and follow-through with audit/inspection findings to resolution as it related to involved CRA staff.
• Assist with other assigned clinical responsibilities within scope of role to provide best practice and/or support to junior clinical staff.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
• Provides site level management for established protocols and portfolio under general supervision
• Provides mentoring/support to CRAs for study related topics
• Identification of development opportunities and provides necessary training to for junior team members as needed
• Co-monitoring with CRAs and support site visits, as needed

Computer Skills:
• Efficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook
• Familiar with industry CTMS and data management systems

• Understands clinical trial processes with a thorough knowledge of ICH and associated regulatory guidelines

• Minimum of 3-4 years of (CRA) monitoring experience in the pharmaceutical or CRO Industry
• Experience in global oncology trials preferred.

• Excellent organizational skills and ability to prioritize and multi-task

General Description:

BeOne is actively seeking an experienced compliance professional at the manager level who brings a proactive, pragmatic, and detail-oriented approach to compliance monitoring and investigations. This role will report to the Director, Compliance Monitoring and Investigations and will support execution of the global annual compliance monitoring program for all regions outside of Greater China, with primary responsibility for managing the North America program.

In this role, you will coordinate risk-based monitoring plans, assign and track monitoring activities, engage regional and cross-functional stakeholders, analyze program data, and support remediation through completion. You will also support the global whistleblower and investigations program through document review, interviews, case management, committee materials, and case reporting, and will lead investigations as assigned.

This position will be in

the United States, either remote or at BeOne’s offices in San Carlos, CA, Hopewell, NJ, or Cambridge, MA.

Essential Functions of the Job:

• Support execution of the global annual compliance monitoring program for all regions outside of Greater China, including live and transactional monitoring activities and country-specific risk assessments.

• Manage the North America annual monitoring program for the United States and Canada, including defining annual monitoring targets based on established criteria and methodology.

• Identify activities eligible for monitoring and assign monitors based on geography, availability, experience, and program needs.

• Track completion of monitoring checklists, observations, remediation, corrective actions, and other follow-up activities; support remediation through completion where required.

• Conduct regular stakeholder meetings to review monitoring progress, observations, trends, and defined corrective action plans.

• Conduct virtual, live, and retrospective monitoring activities as assigned.

• Support region-specific monitoring plans for markets outside North America through stakeholder engagement, progress tracking, and follow-up on monitoring goals.

• Identify and implement opportunities to enhance program infrastructure, including monitoring methodology, checklists, communication templates, training materials, and onboarding resources for monitors.

• Support the global whistleblower and compliance investigations program for all regions outside of Greater China.

• Support investigations through document review, investigative interviews, preparation of disciplinary review committee materials, and drafting of investigation reports.

• Lead compliance investigations as assigned and ensure investigative activities are conducted with integrity, discretion, consistency, and appropriate confidentiality.

• Maintain the case management system to ensure information is accurate and current.

• Support the evaluation of conflicts of interest disclosures and recommend appropriate guidelines or conditions for approved disclosures.

• Assist with management of third-party support partners, including coordination, quality oversight, and follow-up on deliverables.

• Define and maintain meaningful program metrics and analyze data to identify patterns, trends, and emerging risks.

• Escalate significant observations or trends as appropriate and recommend adjustments to monitoring plans or program controls.

• Assist in creating and maintaining dashboards and quarterly reports for compliance committees, the Audit Committee, leadership, and other stakeholders.

• Maintain systems, policies, procedures, work instructions, templates, and other documentation that support the monitoring and investigations programs.

• Support other compliance initiatives as required.

• Perform live monitoring as needed, with domestic travel up to 20%.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree required.

• 5+ years of combined experience in healthcare compliance, auditing, monitoring, investigations, internal audit, or related field; pharmaceutical or biotech industry experience preferred.

• Working knowledge of laws, regulations, and industry codes relevant to the development and commercialization of pharmaceutical products.

• Working knowledge and experience with U.S. healthcare fraud and abuse laws (e.g., Anti-kickback statute, False Claims Act), FDCA, FDA guidance, OIG Compliance Program Guidance, OIG advisory opinions, and federal and state transparency and compliance program disclosure laws, and U.S. and international industry codes (e.g., PhRMA, EFPIA, IFPMA).

• Experience supporting or managing risk-based compliance monitoring programs, including live and transactional activity reviews.

• Experience supporting or conducting internal investigations.

• Experience coordinating multiple workstreams, stakeholders, vendors, deadlines, and corrective action plans in a global, matrixed environment.

• Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive matters with integrity and discretion.

• Acts with a sense of urgency, with high motivation and ability to take initiative, follow through and complete projects in a professional and expeditious manner.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to present information clearly to varied audiences.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and translate findings into practical recommendations.

• Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, initiative, and ability to follow through on commitments in a fast-paced environment.

• Collaborative interpersonal style and demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with colleagues.
